questions.question:
You're giving a presentation, and a few students in the back are yawning, looking at the ceiling, and occasionally checking their phones.

What non-verbal cues are they sending, and what decision should you consider?

options.text: They are deeply concentrating; continue as is.
They are bored or disengaged; try to re-engage them with a question or interactive element.
They are just tired; ignore their behavior.
They are being disrespectful; stop the presentation and reprimand them.

questions.solution:
Given: You're giving a presentation, and a few students in the back are yawning, looking at the ceiling, and occasionally checking their phones.

 
 

 Option
 Statement
 Correctness
 Reasoning
 
 
 
 

 1
 They are deeply concentrating; continue as is.
 Incorrect
 Yawning, looking away, and checking phones are signs fo disengagement, not concentration.
 
 

 2
 They are bored or disengaged; try to re-engage them with a question or interactive element.
 Correct
 These non-verbal cues indicates loss of attention. Asking questions or adding interection can regain their focus.
 
 

 3
 They are just tired; ignore their behavior.
 Incorrect
 Ignoring the signals may cause further loss of attention from the audience.
 
 

 4
 They are being disrespectful; stop the presentation and reprimand them.
 Incorrect
 This reaction is too harsh and may create a negative environment.
 
 

Qualities Projected in this situation: Observation skills, adaptability and Audience engagement. 

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer

questions.question: A train traveling at a constant speed enters a 200-meter tunnel. It takes 10 seconds for the entire train to pass through the tunnel. If the train is 100 meters long, what is the speed of the train in meters per second?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of tunnel = 200 m

Length of train = 100 m

Time taken = 10 s

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

Total distance covered

⇒ Length of train + Length of tunnel

⇒ 100 + 200

⇒ 300 m

Speed

⇒ 300 ÷ 10

⇒ 30 m/s

**∴ Speed of the train = 30 m/s.**

questions.question: In a row, P is 7th from the left and Q is 12th from the right. If they interchange their positions, P becomes 22nd from the left. What is the total number of people in the row?
questions.solution:
According to the question:

P's rank from the left → 7th

Q's rank from the right → 12th

After interchange, P's rank from the left → 22nd

Total number of people = P's rank from the left + After interchange, P's rank from the left - 1

Total number of people = 12 + 22 - 1 → 33

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a row of students, if A is 12th from the left and B is 15th from the right, and there are 7 students between them, find the maximum number of students in the row.
questions.solution:
According to the question:

A's rank from the left → 12th

B's rank from the right → 15th

Number of students between A and B → 7

The maximum number of students in the row → A's rank from the left + B's rank from the right + The maximum number of students in the row

→ 12 + 15 + 7 = 34​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3"

questions.question: In a row of 30 students, if Sneha is 12th from the left and Priya is 15th from the right, how many students are between Sneha and Priya?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total students = 30

Sneha position from left = 12

Priya position from right = 15

So, the students are between Sneha and Priya = Total students - ( Position of Sneha + Position of Priya )

= 30 − ( 12 + 15 )

= 30 − 27 

= 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2da1fcd95e30207b623febdd74ad8b88974d8c8b3874a4b925760c59622bdac.png] 

∴ Number of students between Sneha and Priya = 3.

questions.question:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement:

All planets are stars.

All stars are galaxies.

Conclusions:

I. All planets are galaxies.

II. All galaxies are planets.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe926a6aeb11ba1af42f4c00fecfe7806b6500a7ed78ada46e01b8103ba6b177.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c69fb8fa0b68f8500d25b94ac8df3d8f1b1c3aef89bde8b9ec9f6f951cc83ab.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) All planets are galaxies → Follow (As all planets are stars and all stars are galaxies. As whole planets comes in stars which whole comes in galaxies, therefore it is true.)

(II) All galaxies are planets → Does not follow (As all planets are stars and all stars are galaxies. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1"

questions.question:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the inference that follows.

Statement: The government has announced a new policy to reduce carbon emissions by 50% in the next 10 years.

Inference:

I. The government is taking steps to combat climate change.

II. The new policy will have no impact on the environment.

III. The government is not interested in reducing carbon emissions.

options.text: If both I and II follow
If both I and III follow

questions.solution:
**Given Statement:**

The government has announced a new policy to reduce carbon emissions by 50% in the next 10 years.

**Check the Inferences:**

I. The government is taking steps to combat climate change.

Reducing carbon emissions is a major action to fight climate change.

⇒ This inference follows. ✔

II. The new policy will have no impact on the environment.

The statement only says emissions will be reduced, which normally affects the environment positively.

⇒ Saying no impact is not supported.

⇒ This inference does not follow. ✘

III. The government is not interested in reducing carbon emissions.

The statement clearly says the government wants to reduce emissions by 50%.

⇒ This is the opposite of the statement.

⇒ This inference does not follow. ✘

**∴ Only Inference I follows.**

questions.question: A government bans single-use plastic, claiming it will reduce ocean pollution. Which of the following, if true, best supports this decision?

options.text: Most plastic waste in oceans comes from fishing nets and industrial waste.
Citizens are unaware of recycling methods.
A majority of coastal waste is composed of single-use plastic items.
Plastic alternatives are more expensive and less durable.

questions.solution:
Given: A government bans single-use plastic, claiming it will reduce ocean pollution.

Let's check all the options:

(1) Most plastic waste in oceans comes from fishing nets and industrial waste ⇒ **It does not support the decision ( **This weakens the decision as it shifts blame away from single-use plastic.)

(2) Citizens are unaware of recycling methods ⇒**It does not support the decision. ( ** This is irrelevant to the ban on single-use plastic )

**(3) A majority of coastal waste is composed of single-use plastic items ⇒** **It best supports the decision. ( ** Directly proves that banning single-use plastic will reduce ocean pollution. )

(4) Plastic alternatives are more expensive and less durable ⇒ **It does not support the decision. ( ** This weakens the decision as it shows the ban may not be practical.)

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**
